title: Ripple Prime listed as a Coinbase Derivatives broker distribution partner

confirmed_facts.fact: Coinbase's official Derivatives page lists Ripple Prime among its broker distribution partners.
confirmed_facts.source_context: The page states broker distribution partners provide expanded market access to trade Coinbase Derivatives products, then lists Ripple Prime alongside ABN AMRO, Interactive Brokers, Marex, StoneX and others.

confirmed_facts.fact: The same Coinbase Derivatives page currently lists nano XRP Perp-Style with 500 XRP contract size, 37,924 open-interest contracts and 86,175 daily volume units at capture.
confirmed_facts.limitation: Dynamic page; exact market-data timestamp not exposed. These are contract units, not USD aggregate OI.

confirmed_facts.fact: Ripple's October 28, 2026 institutional announcement describes Ripple Prime as a prime-brokerage platform providing capital efficiencies across liquidity pools, financing, settlement and clearing for event contracts and RWA perpetual futures across trading partners.

interpretation.confirmed: A direct commercial distribution relationship exists between Ripple Prime and Coinbase Derivatives at the general product-suite level.
interpretation.inference: Because Coinbase's same product page lists nano XRP Perp among its contracts, Ripple Prime may provide clients with access to Coinbase's XRP derivatives, subject to its own client/product permissions and jurisdictional eligibility.
not_established: That Ripple Prime currently distributes the nano XRP Perp specifically.
That Ripple Prime or its clients hold, buy or sell XRP as a result of the distribution relationship.
That XRP is accepted as collateral in Ripple Prime's access route.
Any order flow, open interest, revenue share, client count or trading volume attributable to Ripple Prime.
That Ripple Prime uses Coinbase Financial Markets or Deribit for all of its client activity.

competing_hypotheses.thesis: Ripple Prime distribution could expand institutional access to Coinbase-listed XRP derivatives and improve hedging and market-making reach.
competing_hypotheses.disconfirming_evidence: No contract-specific access matrix, order flow or client activity has been disclosed.

competing_hypotheses.thesis: Additional derivatives distribution may increase hedging, basis trades and short exposure without generating net XRP spot purchases.
competing_hypotheses.disconfirming_evidence: If prime-broker clients acquire XRP for collateral or hedging inventory, some incremental spot/custody demand may occur; no balances are disclosed.

competing_hypotheses.thesis: Ripple Prime can distribute Coinbase derivatives while Ripple promotes RLUSD and XRP-based infrastructure; the relationship is complementary at distribution level but competing across stablecoin/collateral choices.
competing_hypotheses.disconfirming_evidence: Actual collateral and settlement preferences by client are unknown.

actual_capital_rule: Broker distribution, derivatives product listings and open interest do not establish net spot XRP purchases. Track product access, collateral inventory, order flow, net exposure and spot execution separately.
next_actions: Seek a Ripple Prime product/venue matrix or official client-facing product notice identifying Coinbase nano XRP Perp access.
Check whether Ripple Prime routes orders through Coinbase Financial Markets, another FCM or a separate broker arrangement.
Determine whether the distribution agreement includes XRP-specific collateral, USD/USDC settlement or cross-margining.
Monitor Coinbase Derivatives product data and Ripple Prime disclosures for product-level volume or client adoption.
Keep any Ripple Prime-related XRP flow feature blocked until product-specific execution or collateral evidence is obtained.
